summary: An R-6 flat-top ground cabin built in 1957 on the Malheur National Forest, replacing a 1929 cupola shelter, still staffed each summer and not available as a public rental.

access.note: Active staffed lookout on the Malheur National Forest, Blue Mountain Ranger District; not a public rental (the forest's rentable lookout is Fall Mountain, not Indian Rock)

visit.trail_note: No drive-up/trail detail found in sources consulted

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service - Malheur National Forest

events.note: Cupola from a standard D-6 lookout house erected as an initial shelter on Indian Rock, for about $85 plus contributed labor
Newspaper item describes a summer lookout staffer heading to Indian Rock Lookout
New wooden ground house (R6 flat top) built by Forest Service crews, replacing the 1929 structure
Vandalism reported: propane tank regulator and copper tubing removed
Crockets Knob Fire burned in August 2022 in the vicinity of Indian Rock; exact impact on the structure unclear from sources reviewed
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, July 3, 2022

evidence.supports: Built 1957 replacing 1929 structure, R6 flat top design
evidence.quote:
Indian Rock was constructed in 1957 replacing an earlier structure built in 1929.
The structure is a USFS R6 Flat Top ground cabin.

evidence.supports: 1929 cupola shelter built for $85 plus labor
evidence.quote: A lookout shelter consisting of the cupola of a standard D-6 lookout house has just been completed on Indian Rock lookout. When a house is built here, the cupola will be raised to complete the cabin -- cost $85 plus contributed time.
Roger Stephen, who just returned home from George Fox college, left Monday morning for Indian Rock Lookout in the Whitman National Forest, near Bates, where he will serve as a lookout for the summer.
A wooden ground house is being constructed by forest service employees on Indian Rock, on the Blue Mountain district.
Some recent examples of vandalism occurring are removal of a propane tank regulator and all copper tubing at Indian Rock Lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1953 newspaper clipping calls it 'Indian Rock Lookout in the Whitman National Forest,' an older forest name; Indian Rock is now administered as part of the Malheur National Forest after a later Forest Service reorganization, consistent with current sources.

notes_for_editor: Sources 2 and 3 are the same page cited for two different facts, as allowed. The Crockets Knob Fire's effect on the structure itself is ambiguous in the only source found (a blog category page, not the full post); a reviewer with time to fetch the individual cherylhill.net post could confirm whether the lookout survived undamaged. Current brief's 'access: unknown' should be updated to reflect that it is an active staffed station, not a rental. Fact-check 2026-10-04: every footnoted sentence in the story checked out against its cited evidence, including the specific month details (December 1929, September 1957) and the 'Blue Mountain Eagle' attribution, none of which appeared verbatim in the evidence excerpts but all of which were confirmed by re-fetching the weebly source directly. The July 3, 2022 NHLR registration date was also confirmed directly against the NHLR page. No unsupported claims or copied wording found; no edits needed.
